vocabulary: A .env-style file was counted inside one or more plugin folders, outside the profile's secret stores. The audit matched file names only and did not open any file, so it cannot tell whether the file holds a real secret.

Copies of config.yaml were counted at the home or profile root and in backup folders; a config.yaml can contain keys typed into it. The audit matched file names and lstat metadata only and did not open any file, so it cannot tell whether any copy holds a key.
Counted apart from work folders because names alone cannot tell test values from real secrets; the audit opened no file.

Files named as copies of a Hermes secret store (such as .env.bak-*, auth.json.old, or a store's name inside a backups folder) were counted next to the live stores or in backup folders. The audit matched file names and lstat metadata only and did not open any file, so it cannot tell whether a copy holds a working secret, an expired one, or none.

Files whose names match secret-store patterns were counted outside the places the Hermes source keeps secrets. The audit matched file names only and did not open any file, so it cannot tell whether any of them holds a real secret; a copy, sync or share of those folders includes them. Files that third-party plugins write are not known to the audit as expected stores and are counted here.

Part of the home could not be listed (a safety cap, an unreadable folder, an undecodable name, or a missing or invalid home path), so the counts are partial. The audit matched file names only and did not open any file; what was not listed is neither clean nor a problem.

Secret-named files carry group or world permission bits (mode & 0o077) in a home whose file modes vary. The audit matched file names and lstat mode bits only and did not open any file, so it cannot tell whether a file holds a real secret or who else can log in to this machine.

Secret-named files were counted inside nested directories shaped like a Hermes home below the profile root. The audit matched file names only and did not open any file, so it cannot tell real secrets from test values.

free_strings.what: absolute path of an existing top-level folder inside the audited home that holds secret-named work-folder files, or the home root itself for files directly at the root; one row per folder with count and classes (pattern class label -> count), sorted by path
free_strings.why_safe: never deeper than the top-level folder and never the path of a secret-named file. EvidenceSerializer.scalar keeps an absolute string whose resolved form exists (Path.resolve + lstat) and returns the resolved path, so it is KEPT AS IS when the home path has no symlinked ancestor (the module never resolves: it reads only os.scandir/os.lstat and joins strings). It must still exist at serialisation time; if it is gone, or a redaction state marks it as overlapping a credential value, the serializer tokenises it.

notes: Envelope: exactly {secret_file_copies, findings, status, coverage, run_metrics}. status is the legacy 'pass'/'fail' from make_component_envelope (always 'pass': no finding maps to severity 'error'); adapt_component_result stores it as legacy_status_ignored. coverage is honoured (could_not_verify when any cut or any could_not_verify finding).

adapt_component_result KEEPS run_metrics: it copies every top-level key except ok/status/error/findings/coverage/classification, so adapted['run_metrics'] == {'elapsed_seconds': <float>}. audit_surface must read res['secret_file_copies'] into measurements and keep res['run_metrics'] OUT of canonical_payload (it differs on every run).
Findings carry affected_identities == []; adapt_component_result does not add the caller's identity to non-error findings.

Digest safety: the section holds no elapsed time and no wall-clock-derived value; backup copy dates are the file mtime as numeric UTC year and month. A run cut by the 15 s time budget (truncated_by 'time_budget') depends on machine speed; that is a coverage limit, reported as such, not hidden.

Free strings: the section emits no string that the serializer tokenises. by_top_level_folder is a list of {path, count, classes}, example_locations a list of {path, class}, plugin_folders_with_dotenv a list of plugin folder paths; every path is an absolute path of an existing folder and every other string is vocabulary. Tests prove the serializer returns each path unchanged, no dict with an 'hmac' field (or 'hmac:' sealed key) appears in the sealed section or the persisted findings, and two runs with fresh serializers give identical sealed sections and findings. Caveat: the serializer returns Path.resolve() of a path, so a home reached through a symlinked ancestor is stored in its resolved form (still identical across runs).

Persistence without the shared-set additions: finding_dto drops evidence keys not in _EVIDENCE_NUMERIC_KEYS/_EVIDENCE_VOCAB_KEYS (currently only count, cuts, reason survive) and replaces every secret_file_copies consequence with DEFAULT_FINDING_CONSEQUENCE because none is in ALLOWED_FINDING_CONSEQUENCES. Add numeric_evidence_keys to _EVIDENCE_NUMERIC_KEYS, 'truncated_by' to _EVIDENCE_VOCAB_KEYS, the rule ids to RULE_IDS and the consequences to FINDING_CONSEQUENCES.

'secret_file_copies' is in schema_keys (the section is stored under canonical_payload['secret_file_copies']) AND in vocabulary (component_dto serializes component_id as a value; without it component_id becomes a token); expected-kind and pattern-class names appear as dict keys and as values, so they are in both lists.
'limit_exceeded' is a defensive fallback for could_not_verify.truncated_by and is not reachable from a real walk.
Module reads no config.yaml and no credential file: only os.scandir and os.lstat (re-confirmed by test_wire_only_lstat_and_scandir_after_import).
